question:
The prices, in rupees, of one notebook, one pen, and one file are represented by $x$, $y$, and $z$, respectively. The following purchase information is available:
$$x+y+z=90$$
$$2x+3y+z=170$$
$$3x+y+2z=170$$

(a) Evaluate the determinant of the coefficient matrix and determine whether the prices are uniquely determined.

(b) Solve the system to find $x$, $y$, and $z$.

(c) Verify the prices using all three purchase equations.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient matrix is
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\2 & 3 & 1\\3 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
Its determinant is
$$|A|=1(6-1)-1(4-3)+1(2-9)$$
$$|A|=5-1-7=-3$$
Since $|A|\neq0$, the system is consistent and the prices are uniquely determined.

(b)
Subtracting the first equation from the second equation gives
$$x+2y=80$$
Subtracting twice the first equation from the third equation gives
$$x-y=-10$$
Thus,
$$x=y-10$$
Substituting in $x+2y=80$,
$$y-10+2y=80$$
$$3y=90$$
$$y=30$$
Therefore,
$$x=30-10=20$$
Using $x+y+z=90$,
$$20+30+z=90$$
$$z=40$$
Hence, the prices are $x=20$, $y=30$, and $z=40$.

(c)
Verification:
$$20+30+40=90$$
$$2(20)+3(30)+40=40+90+40=170$$
$$3(20)+30+2(40)=60+30+80=170$$
Thus, the solution satisfies all three equations.

options.A:
(a) $|A|=-3$, so the prices are uniquely determined
(b) $(x,y,z)=(20,30,40)$
(c) All three purchase equations are satisfied
options.C:
(a) $|A|=0$, so the prices are not uniquely determined
(b) $(20,30,40)$ is one of infinitely many solutions
(c) The equations are dependent
options.D:
(a) $|A|=-3$
(b) $(x,y,z)=(20,40,30)$
(c) Only the first equation is satisfied
